title: Melanoma: Uveal
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Melanoma: Uveal. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Ophthalmologic Workup (dilated funduscopy, slit-lamp biomicroscopy, B-scan ultrasonography with tumor thickness and basal dimensions, OCT, widefield fundus photography, liver-directed metastatic screening with multiphase liver MRI, HLA-A*02:01 genotyping, prognostic GEP and Monosomy 3 / BAP1 profiling, baseline LFTs and LDH) -> Stage and HLA Stratification (primary localized non-metastatic vs high-risk surveillance GEP Class 2 / Monosomy 3 M0 vs metastatic HLA-A*02:01 positive vs metastatic HLA-A*02:01 negative or Tebentafusp progressor) -> Localized eye-preserving radiotherapy (plaque brachytherapy or proton beam, enucleation for large advanced or blind painful eye) -> High-risk intensive liver MRI surveillance with adjuvant trial enrollment -> Metastatic HLA-positive first-line Tebentafusp step-up weekly therapy (IMCgp100-202) -> Metastatic HLA-negative liver-directed therapy (PHP, HAI, TACE, Y-90 SIRT) or nivolumab plus ipilimumab. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Melanoma: Uveal Version 2.2026.

a.text: Dedicated multiphase liver MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging is the preferred metastatic screening and surveillance modality because more than 90% of initial uveal melanoma metastases involve the liver; abdominal CT with contrast is an alternative when MRI is unavailable or contraindicated.

b.text: HLA-A*02:01 allele genotyping is a mandatory companion diagnostic before first-line systemic therapy for metastatic disease because Tebentafusp eligibility requires HLA-A*02:01 positivity.

c.text: Prognostic profiling (GEP Class 1A/1B low risk vs Class 2 high risk; Monosomy 3 and BAP1 loss) on biopsied or enucleated tumor tissue stratifies metastatic risk and selects high-risk patients for intensive liver surveillance and adjuvant trial enrollment.

d.text: Eye-preserving radiotherapy (plaque brachytherapy I-125 or Ru-106 delivering 85 Gy to tumor apex, or proton beam radiotherapy) achieves greater than 95% local tumor control; primary enucleation is reserved for large advanced tumors, extensive extrascleral extension, or a blind and painful eye.

e.text: Tebentafusp-tebn (bispecific gp100 x CD3 ImmTAC, IMCgp100-202 trial) showed significant overall survival benefit versus investigator choice in HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma; step-up dosing with in-hospital monitoring for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is required for the initial 3 doses, then 68 mcg IV weekly until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Melanoma: Uveal - Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the clinical workup before stage and HLA stratification. Confirm ocular diagnosis with funduscopy, biomicroscopy, ultrasound dimensions, OCT and photography; screen the liver for metastases; obtain mandatory HLA-A*02:01 genotype and prognostic profiling; and document baseline liver laboratories.
bullets: Comprehensive ophthalmologic evaluation: dilated funduscopy, slit-lamp biomicroscopy, and high-resolution B-scan ocular ultrasonography (tumor thickness, basal dimensions)
Diagnostic optical coherence tomography (OCT) and widefield fundus photography
Liver-directed metastatic screening: dedicated multiphase liver MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (preferred; >90% initial metastases occur in liver) or abdominal CT with contrast
Mandatory molecular testing: HLA-A*02:01 allele genotype testing (essential companion diagnostic for Tebentafusp eligibility)
Prognostic genetic profiling on tumor tissue (if biopsied or enucleated): Gene Expression Profiling (GEP Class 1A/1B low risk vs Class 2 high risk) and Monosomy 3 / BAP1 mutation analysis
Baseline systemic laboratory assessment: LFTs (alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT, total bilirubin, LDH)

nodes.name: Stage and HLA Stratification
nodes.title: Melanoma: Uveal - Stage and HLA Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign localized vs high-risk surveillance vs metastatic HLA-A*02:01 positive vs metastatic HLA-A*02:01 negative disease; the group selects the eye-preserving, surveillance, Tebentafusp, or liver-directed and immunotherapy pathway.
nodes.path: Melanoma: Uveal / Stage and HLA Stratification
bullets: Primary localized disease: small, medium, or large choroidal or ciliary body melanoma without distant metastases (M0).
High-risk surveillance group: GEP Class 2, Monosomy 3, or large apical thickness with no distant metastases (M0).
Metastatic HLA-A*02:01 positive disease: distant metastases with companion diagnostic confirming HLA-A*02:01 positivity.
Metastatic HLA-A*02:01 negative disease (or progressor on Tebentafusp): distant metastases without HLA-A*02:01, or progression after Tebentafusp.

nodes.name: Localized Treatment
nodes.title: Localized Uveal Melanoma: Plaque or Proton Radiotherapy vs Enucleation
nodes.description: Eye-preserving radiotherapy is preferred for primary localized choroidal or ciliary body melanoma; primary enucleation is reserved for large advanced tumors, extensive extrascleral extension, or a blind and painful eye.
bullets: Eye-preserving radiotherapy preferred: Plaque Brachytherapy (I-125 or Ru-106 delivering 85 Gy to tumor apex) or Proton Beam Radiotherapy (PBRT) achieving >95% local tumor control.
Select plaque vs proton technique by tumor size, location (choroidal vs ciliary body), and proximity to optic disc and fovea in multidisciplinary ocular oncology consultation.
Primary enucleation reserved strictly for large advanced tumors, extensive extrascleral extension, or blind/painful eye.
Surveillance after definitive local therapy: dilated ophthalmologic examination plus dedicated liver imaging per high-risk features; offer clinical trial enrollment where eligible.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Plaque Brachytherapy (I-125 / Ru-106) or Proton Radiotherapy vs Enucleation

nodes.name: High-Risk Surveillance
nodes.title: High-Risk Uveal Melanoma: Intensive Liver Surveillance +/- Adjuvant Trials
nodes.description: Intensive liver-directed imaging surveillance for high-risk GEP Class 2, Monosomy 3, or large apical thickness M0 disease, with enrollment in adjuvant targeted or immunotherapy trials.
bullets: Intensive liver-directed imaging surveillance: dedicated multiphase liver MRI (or liver ultrasound/CT where MRI is unavailable) every 3 to 6 months for 5 to 10 years.
Enrollment in clinical trials of adjuvant targeted/immunotherapy for high-risk GEP Class 2 / Monosomy 3 patients.
Continue dilated ophthalmologic follow-up after definitive eye therapy alongside systemic surveillance.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: High-Intensity Liver MRI Surveillance (q3-6 months) +/- Adjuvant Clinical Trials

nodes.name: Metastatic HLA-Positive Treatment
nodes.title: Metastatic HLA-A*02:01 Positive: Tebentafusp Weekly
nodes.description: First-line Tebentafusp-tebn step-up weekly therapy for HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma with CRS monitoring for initial doses.
nodes.path: Melanoma: Uveal / Metastatic HLA-A*02:01 Positive / Treatment
bullets: First-line Systemic Therapy: Tebentafusp-tebn (bispecific gp100 x CD3 T-cell redirecting ImmTAC): Step-up dosing: 20 mcg IV day 1, 30 mcg IV day 8, 68 mcg IV day 15, followed by 68 mcg IV weekly until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity (IMCgp100-202 trial; significant overall survival benefit vs investigator choice).
In-hospital monitoring for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) required for initial 3 doses; monitor for rash, pruritus, hypotension, hypoxia, and liver enzyme elevation.
Confirm HLA-A*02:01 positivity with companion diagnostic before first dose; reassess with liver-directed imaging on therapy.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Tebentafusp 68 mcg IV Weekly (Step-up: 20mcg d1, 30mcg d8, 68mcg d15) for HLA-A*02:01+

nodes.name: Metastatic HLA-Negative Treatment
nodes.title: Metastatic HLA-A*02:01 Negative: Liver-Directed Therapy or Nivolumab + Ipilimumab
nodes.description: Liver-directed and systemic combination therapy for HLA-A*02:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma or progressors on Tebentafusp.
nodes.path: Melanoma: Uveal / Metastatic HLA-A*02:01 Negative / Treatment
bullets: Liver-dominant disease: Percutaneous hepatic perfusion (PHP with Melphalan), Hepatic arterial infusion (HAI), Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), or Y-90 Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (SIRT) selected by liver tumor burden, extrahepatic spread, and center expertise.
Systemic immunotherapy: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + Ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV q3w x 4 cycles -> Nivolumab maintenance (clinical benefit in select patients); monitor for immune-related adverse events.
Alternative: clinical trials (PKC/MEK inhibitors) offered at every line, especially for rapid progressors or extrahepatic disease.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Liver-Directed Therapy (PHP / TACE / Y-90 SIRT) or Nivolumab + Ipilimumab
